hook_text: The phone in your hand connects you to the world and poisons a dump in two years. Both are true.
clip_script: Put six ordinary things on a table. A nappy, a phone, a cold-drink bottle, a noodle packet, a tyre, a lighter. Every one solved a problem. Every one made a new one. That is the negative impact of technology. To find it, follow one product through its life: raw materials, making, transport, use, throwing away. At each stop ask three questions: what does this do to the earth, to people, to the person using it? The cold-drink bottle: oil, energy, trucks, sugar that rots teeth, then a drain or a dump for five hundred years. Where is the harm worst? That is where you aim the fix. Six directions: change the material, the design, the use, the end of life, the rules, or behaviour. Test each fix with three questions: less harm? same benefit? will it actually work here? Pick your product. The rest of the term, you design against it.
visual_style: Six objects on a whiteboard table; one lifts and travels along a five-stop life-cycle line with three icons at each stop; a bar grows tallest at disposal; six arrows labelled with fix types point at it.
pacing: Table, the three questions, the bottle's journey, six fixes, the choice.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and trace one product you used today through its five life stages.
